The St. Lawrence River is one of the most important waterways in Canada (and North America).
It runs for 3,058 kilometres and has the second-highest discharge of any river in North America after the Mississippi River.
The source is Lake Ontario. 🧵4/15

Flowing from Kingston, around Island of Montreal & past Quebec City to the Gulf of St Lawrence, the River St. Lawrence carries the Great Lakes fresh water to Ocean. If Quebec & Ontario are looking for common cause, look no further than we drink the same water.

The Gulf of Saint Lawrence of Canada has warmed and lost oxygen faster than almost anywhere else in the oceans of the planet. The broad, biologically-rich waterway in eastern Canada drains North America’s Great Lakes, where much human activity takes place...
